newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leonean and Nigerian troops clash.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leonean and Nigerian troops clash.

text.p: Nigerian troops and soldiers loyal to Sierra Leone's military rulers clashed on Saturday south of the capital Freetown, military sources said.
The cause of the clash at Djui, 15 miles (20 km) from the city, was not immediately clear. One source spoke of casualites.

The two sides clashed last Wednesday at Lungi airport across an estuary from the capital as members of the People's Army -- soldiers who backed a May 25 coup and their rebel allies -- hunted for a clandestine radio station that has broadcast messages from ousted president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
Nigeria, which had troops in the country under a West African defence pact before the coup, has since reinforced as part of efforts to persuade the military junta to restore Kabbah to power.
Impoverished Sierra Leone's West African neighbours have agreed to try dialogue and economic sanctions as methods of persuasion but have retained the military option.
Kabbah came to power in 1996 after multi-party elections ended four years of military rule. Rebels, who took up arms in 1991, rallied to the coup -- the third in five years.
